body.text:
Here's this morning's status, all good news:

**The overnight mystery resolved itself in the best way** — the instrumented dogfood run completed about 25 minutes after your usage ran out: full first index of this repo (716 code chunks, 13 ledger entries, 12 session summaries), `DONE_OK` in the log. The original stall's root cause is now baked into the design: the first attempt made one giant embed call with no observable progress; reindex now batches with durable checkpoints after every batch, so progress is always visible and a killed run resumes nearly free.

**M10 is verified and committed.** I re-ran the full CLI suite (101 tests passing, 17 new), reviewed the implementation — the judgment calls are genuinely good, including a per-user durable model cache so the 162 MB download never repeats, and diff-driven incrementality — and proved it live: the second pass since the dogfood embedded **only the 2 chunks** the intervening commit touched, out of 700+.

**`git for-ai report` is now a real command.** I wired it into the CLI alongside reindex; `git for-ai report` regenerates your `.git-for-ai\report.html` on demand (now including today's commits), with `--since`, `-n`, and `--md` variants.

**Everything is pushed.** All of yesterday's and this morning's commits plus the three intent refs are on GitHub — the backup loop is closed.

**M11 is underway** — a background agent is building the hybrid query engine (vector + keyword retrieval fused by rank, blame-position filtering, Anthropic-API synthesis with a clean no-key fallback), under your RAM rule: no real model in its tests, nothing heavy in parallel. When it lands, M12 wires `ask` and `blame --why` — and then the searchable index your machine spent yesterday evening building becomes something you can actually interrogate: "why is this line like this?" answered from intent, sessions, and code together.
This README says "no actual implementation logic yet" — two days out of date. Restructuring now: history to `architecture/history/`, README rewritten for a human reader:

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && sed -i 's|^### M9 — Embeddings: chunking, provider, vector store$|### M9 — Embeddings: chunking, provider, vector store ✅ DONE (commit `6632bf8`) — node:sqlite + sqlite-vec, superseding the better-sqlite3 wording below|; s|^### M10 — `cli reindex`$|### M10 — `cli reindex` ✅ DONE (commit `37f6315`) — dogfooded on this repo with the real model|' architecture/CLI_PLAN.md && grep -n "^### M9\|^### M10" architecture/CLI_PLAN.md

body.text: Now capturing the old README's history narrative into the archive, then the rewrite:

attributes.command:
cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add README.md architecture/CLI_PLAN.md architecture/PLAN_2026-07-18.md architecture/history/ && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Docs refresh: human-focused README; archive history; update plan status

README rewritten as a project page for a human reader: what git-for-ai
is for (source control that remembers why), the two convictions behind
it (agents should record more than a diff; humans must be able to
review what agents did), a what-works-today command table, quick
start, privacy defaults, and a documentation map. The origin-story and
process narrative moved to architecture/history/PROJECT_GENESIS.md,
alongside the archived session handoff/resume notes.

CLI_PLAN.md: M9/M10 marked done; status banner now points at
PLAN_2026-07-18.md as the authoritative ordering and ./history/ for
session notes. PLAN_2026-07-18.md gains a progress banner (W1 done,
report shipped early, M11 in progress).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && ls architecture/ && git log --oneline -1
